name: Seagulls cap

purpose.for: Islanders who work bare-headed under the Okinawan sun on the quay and the boats (Kōji at the catch tables first; Haru, Masaru and Uncle Kinjō), and the Minato Seagulls' fans who follow the autumn fixtures from the izakaya counter (Daichi, who dreams of a perfect game).
purpose.why: A peak against the glare off the water at the morning catch, cloth that breathes in the heat, a strap that fits any head; and the home team's gull, the same night navy as the jersey on the wall at Sato Ramen, so the whole counter can see whose side you are on.
purpose.where: On the cap rack at Sakura Shōten, hung on its pegs by the strap, a season line near the window where the walk from the door to the till passes it; and on the heads of whoever bought one (src/avatars/hat-assets.js fits it to any head).

notes: Johansson Headwear's JH-605, a 1990s six-panel snapback, built in Blender from a script (site: johansson-town/assets/catalog/seagulls-cap/source/build-seagulls-cap.py, with the .blend). Every measurement is a real cap's (57.5 cm band, 7 cm bill, 1.6 cm button, an eyelet per panel two thirds up, a 6.5 by 4 cm opening, seven-stud straps), scaled to the head it is worn on: the town's default adult (Rh 0.2406 m), so it is the size Sakura sells and a resident wears; World fits it to any other head from the head recorded in the model's extras (wear). The cloth material's vertex colour is a shade of the wearer's hatColour: one model is a navy, a white or a green cap. Colours from World's palettes (ISLAND_PALETTE): the team's Night navy, Paper white, Turmeric yellow; the green undervisor of the period.

checks.detail: Who it is for, why they want it and where it belongs are written down.
